edits.before: Location. Corollary 4.15 and Remark 4.16, page 54; the repeated conclusion on page 55; corresponding introduction statement. The corollary puts \(L_{\mathfrak f}(\chi,0)/c^+_\tau\) in \(\overline\mathbb Q^\times\), with no nonvanishing hypothesis.
edits.after: Location. Corollary 4.15 and Remark 4.16, page 54; the repeated conclusion on page 55; corresponding introduction statement. The corollary puts \(L_{\mathfrak f}(\chi,0)/c^+_\tau\) in \(\overline{\mathbb Q}^\times\), with no nonvanishing hypothesis.

edits.before: Deligne’s period is nonzero, so the ratio in the corollary is zero, which is not in \(\overline\mathbb Q^\times\). Counterevidence and repair. The period comparison itself is a comparison of nonzero periods and can remain in \(\mathbb C^\times/\overline\mathbb Q^\times\). The \(L\)-value conclusion should be in \(\overline\mathbb Q\), or explicitly assume nonvanishing. Theorem 4.10 permits zero, and its integrality assertion is not refuted by this example. This is a mathematical boundary-case correction, not a complaint about a missing reference.
